chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Musa ibn Ibrahim al-Muharabi, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Musa ibn Abdullah, from Maymun ibn Ali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'A person's self-admiration is an indication of the weakness of his intellect.'

key_terms.إعجاب: Self-admiration, conceit, excessive self-satisfaction ('ujb) — a recognized spiritual vice in Islamic ethics
key_terms.النفس: The self, soul — here referring to one's own ego or person
key_terms.ضعف العقل: Weakness of intellect — the inability to perceive one's own faults and limitations

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about self-admiration and intellect?
ai.summary: Imam Sadiq (peace be upon him) reports a saying of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) condemning self-conceit ('ujb) as a sign of intellectual weakness. This teaching addresses the vice of vanity and excessive self-satisfaction, which in classical Islamic ethics was seen as a barrier to spiritual growth and sound judgment. The audience — students of the Imam's circle — would have understood 'ujb as a recognized spiritual disease to be overcome through self-awareness and humility.
